messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 14:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call exec recap: Acme Corp — leadership next steps

Thanks all — quick executive recap from our call today with Jenna and the Acme leadership team. TL;DR: strong business case, primary goal is to reduce search/response latency for internal agent workflows and cut per-ticket AI cost by ~40% via model/caching optimizations and a dedicated inference plan.

Key business outcomes discussed:
- Reduce avg response time for internal search from ~1.8s -> target 300-600ms for priority flows (customer support + fraud ops).
- Cut inference unit cost ~30-45% by using Redwood Dedicated with batching and KV prefix caching; Acme wants predictable monthly spend.
- Compliance: data residency for EU customers is not in scope for initial phase, but they asked for audit log / access controls for PII handling.

Primary risks / open items:
1) Procurement path: Acme procurement expects a standard SOW + PO. Jenna said procurement will need an enterprise contact for contract/legal redlines and a preliminary quote by next Wed (2027-08-25).
2) Security/compliance: they requested SOC 2 Type II evidence and an outline of retention controls and KMS options.
3) Capacity/SLAs: they want confirmation we can guarantee throughput for a dedicated pool for their pilot (50k reqs/day with 95th pct latency SLO).

Next steps (owners / ETA):
- Marissa (me): share tailored MVP plan + cost estimate and SOW draft — by Wed 2027-08-25. (Attachment: Acme_Redwood_MVP_Plan_v1.pdf)
- Sean: technical follow-up to map priority flows and expected QPS + token estimates — by Fri 2027-08-20.
- Jenna / Acme: provide procurement contact and initial headcount for pilot ops, confirm compliance checklist items — by Tue 2027-08-24.
- Laura: leadership note re: any commercial flexibility (credits / shorter commit) if procurement needs a pilot-friendly term — ASR (as soon as reasonable).

Ask for execs: Laura, appreciate a quick read and sign-off on the recommended commercial flexibility (I suggest offering a 3-month pilot discount tier or a credit buffer to accelerate procurement). If you approve, I’ll include that in the SOW draft.

Attachment: Acme_Redwood_MVP_Plan_v1.pdf (1.2MB, PDF) — quick scope, milestones, and uplift/cost model.

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great recap and aligned on the priorities. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Procurement contact is Priya Menon (procurement@acme.com). She will need the SOW + a commercial quote with clear monthly committed spend and a line-item for pilot credits.
- Security ask: SOC 2 Type II report is required; also please include a short note on encryption at rest and KMS integration options. We can share a security questionnaire if helpful.
- Pilot acceptance criteria: 1) sustained 95th pct latency <700ms for critical flows over a 7-day window; 2) no more than 2 production incidents attributable to inference infra during pilot; 3) delivery of audit logs for pilot traffic.

We’ll aim to get Priya looped in by EOD Wed (2027-08-18). I’ll confirm headcount for the pilot next week.

On the commercial ask, Priya will want to see either a month-to-month pilot with a capped spend or a 3-month commit with a discount. Both are options for us to consider.

Thanks,
Jenna Park
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Corp
